title: All In the Mind with Sana Qadar - ABC listen
description: All in the Mind is an exploration of the mental: the mind, brain and behaviour — everything from addiction to artificial intelligence.

episodes.title: Staying sane in space
episodes.description: In the last couple of weeks, a lot of people have been getting excited about space exploration thanks to Artemis II.
episodes.narrativeHook: Artemis II's launch sparks renewed interest in space exploration and its psychological challenges.

episodes.title: Mind Hacks with Dr Billy Garvey: "being a bit kinder to myself"
episodes.description: Welcome back to All in the Mind's little sister: Mind Hacks.
episodes.narrativeHook: Dr. Billy Garvey explores self-compassion in this Mind Hacks episode.

episodes.title: Tantrums, sleep training and anxiety: Dr Billy Garvey answers your parenting questions
episodes.description: How can I help my child with anxiety? What's the deal with sleep training? Are we supposed to ignore tantrums?

episodes.title: The psychology of masturbation
episodes.description: This week we're talking about something intimate… and sometimes taboo: masturbation.

episodes.title: Mind Hacks: Casey Beros
episodes.description: Welcome back to All in the Mind's little sister: Mind Hacks.

episodes.title: Tough conversations and anticipatory grief: being a carer
episodes.description: When Casey Beros' dad was diagnosed with mesothelioma, she knew her entire world would change.

episodes.title: Family estrangement and infidelity: Esther Perel answers your questions
episodes.description: How do you grieve a dying parent you're estranged from? Do cheaters ever change? People say love should feel 'easy', is that true?

episodes.title: Mind Hacks: Joel Pearson
episodes.description: Welcome back to All in the Mind's little sister: Mind Hacks. In this episode, cognitive neuroscientist Joel Pearson tells us how he manages his own stress (clue: it involves saunas!)

episodes.title: Is AI making our brains lazier?
episodes.description: Social media gave us brain rot; will AI give us cognitive atrophy? How can we possibly learn to cope with the sheer amount of uncertainty and change heading our way?

episodes.title: Mind Hacks: Esther Perel
episodes.description: Introducing All in the Mind's little sister: Mind Hacks. Each week, we'll bring you bonus content with special guests, featuring rapid fire questions about their mental health tips and pet peeves. It's like a psychology version of eff, marry kill!

narrativeHook: Dive into the mind, brain, and behavior with topics ranging from addiction to AI.

title: Background Briefing - ABC listen
description: The Background Briefing podcast brings you true stories not everyone will want you to hear, told by trusted reporters across Australia.

episodes.title: 01 In Search of the Missing Artist | The sculptor
episodes.description: The sales pitch goes that Jean Paul Mangin is a reclusive Parisian sculptor whose works are internationally acclaimed. His pieces sell quickly through one particular Australian gallery, sought after by trendy interior designers.
episodes.narrativeHook: A reclusive Parisian sculptor's mysterious works captivate the art world through an Australian gallery.

episodes.title: Introducing | In Search of the Missing Artist
episodes.description: For years, art buyers have been told that this man is an internationally acclaimed, intensely private Parisian sculptor. His bold, brightly coloured plastic works are available through one Melbourne gallery, and they're selling fast.
episodes.narrativeHook: A mysterious Parisian sculptor's vibrant plastic works captivate Melbourne's art scene.

episodes.title: 03 The Road to Bondi | Deepfake
episodes.description: How did a wounded Bondi survivor become the face of a global deepfake conspiracy in less than 24 hours? Arsen Ostrovsky was celebrating Chanukah at Bondi Beach when the first shots rang out.

episodes.title: 02 The Road to Bondi | A Test of Character
episodes.description: This man fled Iran after being imprisoned and tortured for protesting the regime. Known only as AB, he came to Australia hoping to start again — and, in many ways, he did. He found love and started a family.

episodes.title: 01 The Road to Bondi | Father and Son
episodes.description: You think you know the story. You know how it ended. But you don’t know how it began. In the first episode of The Road to Bondi, reporter Josh Robertson traces the decades-long path that led a father and son to carry out their plan.

episodes.title: TRAILER — Introducing The Road to Bondi
episodes.description: In an ordinary Australian suburb, a father and son are secretly planning something terrible. One fateful summer evening, their path brings them crashing into the lives of strangers from around the world whose own stories haven’t yet been told.

episodes.title: 06 Hometown Boys | Not the only one
episodes.description: Insiders from the Harrow-Balmoral football club decide to break the code of silence. For Elise, it’s time to rebuild her life. But her story inspires other women to emerge with their own troubling accounts of the town’s club culture.

episodes.title: 05 Hometown Boys | 'Luke, Maybe'
episodes.description: A key witness submits a startling new statement that topples the guilty verdict and forces a retrial. This time, the men accused will not give evidence. But Lisa Hutchins, the trusted bush nurse will take the stand again — now for the defence.

episodes.title: 04 Hometown Boys | The Trial
episodes.description: As the criminal trial unfolds, witnesses from Balmoral waver on the stand, and the judge is "taken aback". The courtroom is heaving with supporters of the accused but the verdict is not what they're expecting.

episodes.title: 03 Hometown Boys | The 'Mayoress of Balmoral'
episodes.description: A respected bush nurse with close ties to the accused becomes a key police witness. As the investigation quietly gathers pace, locals start to choose sides and the family of the victim feels ostracised.

narrativeHook: True stories from trusted Australian reporters reveal hidden truths you won't want to miss.

title: Bludging on the Blindside with Rampaging Roy Slaven and HG Nelson - ABC listen
description: The master of midfield mayhem Rampaging Roy Slaven and the leading light of long shots HG Nelson cast a collective eye over the world of sport.

episodes.title: Shark Meltdown - 30 year celebration.
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and HG discuss the Kevvie-ists parallel world view, the six again rule is out of control and funky Jason Day's walking cool.
episodes.narrativeHook: Roy and HG celebrate 30 years with a chaotic discussion on Kevvie-ists, the six again rule, and funky Jason Day's cool walk.

episodes.title: Happy Easter, happy Rugby League!
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and HG discuss the small mindedness of a Manly fan, Wayne Bennett's chooks at the Easter Show and listening to a podcast in your dreams.
episodes.narrativeHook: Roy and HG discuss Manly fan pettiness, Wayne Bennett's Easter Show chooks, and dreaming of podcasts.

episodes.title: Win, Win, Win! Thank you ABC
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and HG discuss the Kevvie-ists movement at the Broncos, how rugby league could bring peace to the world, and Papenhuyzen's new career as a golf caddy.

episodes.title: Rooting King vs Alex Johnston in a race
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and HG discuss the poor maintenance of our stadiums, whether Wayne Bennett needs to celebrate rather than sulk, and if Gorden Tallis has become a problem for the Broncos.

episodes.title: Heritage Toilet Lager - Easy drinking
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and HG discuss a possible Rugby League opening ceremony, Rugby League happiness differs from everyday happiness and do we understand the Rugby League expansion master plan?

episodes.title: Celebration of rubber
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and HG discuss applying logic to rugby league, teams must solve their problems on the field and is Rugby League supervised violence?

episodes.title: Mongrel downstairs, pole in the hand
episodes.description: Bludging on the Blindside is back for 2026! In this week's episode, Roy and HG discuss the return of Rugby League to Las Vegas, the feral pig problem in the country, and whether wisdom is the greatest enemy of Rugby League.

episodes.title: 2026: Can't wait!
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, the last show for 2025. Roy and H.G discuss the you beaut ute boot sale, Sydney's celebration of rubber and when is Four Corners going to do a gambling story about the winners?

episodes.title: The race that stops the world
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and H.G discuss the new player in the Australian car industry, Hastie Car Corporation. Gus Gould takes a selfie in the toilet and Bunnings Island is a reality, Loloata Island in PNG.

episodes.title: Teddy Swims to the toilet
episodes.description: This week on Bludging on the Blindside, Roy and HG discuss the Broncos and Reece Walsh's stunning performance at the NRL Grand Final, Teddy Swims visits the heritage listed toilets and the 'Year of healing' for Manly ended last weekend.

narrativeHook: Rampaging Roy Slaven and HG Nelson bring their unique perspectives to the world of sport in this dynamic podcast.

title: Conversations with Richard Fidler and Sarah Kanowski - ABC listen
description: Conversations draws you deeper into the life story of someone you may, or may not, have heard about — someone who has seen and done amazing things.

episodes.title: 'The century of foundlings'—what Cynthia found when she went looking maternal family secrets
episodes.description: Writer Cynthia Banham on discovering the shocking truth about her great-grandmother, reckoning with buried family secrets, and the criticisms mothers face from others and sometimes most harshly, from themselves.
episodes.narrativeHook: Writer Cynthia Banham uncovers shocking family secrets about her great-grandmother and confronts the harsh criticisms faced by mothers.

episodes.title: Spotting the psychopaths, sadists and narcissists in our lives and how to get rid of them
episodes.description: Toxic people are around us in our workplaces, our families and our dating lives. Research psychologist Leanne ten Brinke is here to tell you how to spot them, and get rid of them from your orbit.
episodes.narrativeHook: Learn to identify and eliminate toxic people like psychopaths and narcissists from your life.

episodes.title: Encore: How his ex-wife's hidden letter changed everything for Teddy Tahu Rhodes
episodes.description: Born with a magnificent voice, Opera star Teddy Tahu Rhodes fought against his destiny for years until a letter he'd been avoiding reading changed everything (R)

episodes.title: The GP clinic for patients often overlooked by society
episodes.description: Dr Nada Andric wants to improve the health of people who are marginalised in the community and their access to healthcare.

episodes.title: Encore: Bo Seo on good arguments and the power of disagreement
episodes.description: Two-time World Debating champion Bo Seo on how love and listening can improve how we disagree, so we're not at each other's throats online and offline (R). When Bo was 8 years old, he and his parents migrated from Korea to Australia.

episodes.title: Exploring loss, love and meaning with psychoanalyst Stephen Grosz
episodes.description: Stephen Grosz has welcomed people into his office for more than 40 years, and believes our greatest task in life is to see ourselves and others with more clarity, in order to live more easily and with more please.

episodes.title: When the magical worlds of Alice Springs and Prague collided
episodes.description: Writer Tanya Heaslip on swapping life on an Alice Springs station for the fairytale streets of Prague, and the remarkable parallels she found between these two magical worlds.

episodes.title: Encore: Remembering cultural leader and storyteller Rhoda Roberts
episodes.description: The late Widjabul Wieybal woman of the Bundjalung Nation Rhoda Roberts lived through great loss and grief, in the midst of becoming one of Australia's most influential cultural leaders in the arts (R).

episodes.title: Burnout and the 'Bureaucrapper' — how Nick went from the edge of homelessness to helping others
episodes.description: Nick Orchard on how a tough childhood, mental health issues, couch surfing and hip hop have helped him learn how to help others recover from burnout and impostor syndrome.

episodes.title: Encore: The real life story behind 'Looking for Alibrandi'
episodes.description: Melina Marchetta grew up in Sydney in a close-knit Sicilian family, but she never wanted to be seen as 'that Italian girl'. Years later, she drew on her story to write an Australian classic (R).

narrativeHook: Dive into the extraordinary lives of fascinating individuals through intimate and thought-provoking conversations.

title: Expanse with Dominique Bayens - ABC listen
description: In 1999 a young American dumped his bicycle and walked out into the Great Sandy Desert in remote northern Australia. He was an Alaskan firefighter, seemingly with everything to live for. So why did he risk it all to go into the wilderness alone? And how do you search for someone who doesn't want to be found? New episodes released each Wednesday

episodes.title: 06 Expanse: The Nannup Four | Northcliffe
episodes.description: A family friend and former policeman continues to search for answers for Jim and Cath McDougall decades after the Nannup four vanished. The family and friends of Chantelle McDougall try to find their own answers, as one last glimmer of hope emerges.
episodes.narrativeHook: A former policeman searches for answers decades after the Nannup four vanished, as their family finds new hope.

episodes.title: 05 Expanse: The Nannup Four | Simon says
episodes.description: Jim and Cath McDougall are left reeling as the true depth of Simon Kadwill’s deception is revealed.
episodes.narrativeHook: Jim and Cath McDougall confront Simon Kadwill's shocking deception in Expanse: The Nannup Four.

episodes.title: 04 Expanse: The Nannup Four | A question of belief
episodes.description: Tony Popic is talking about an end of days, Simon is seeing spirits and Chantelle is forced into a difficult decision as increasingly troubling hints something's not right come to light.

episodes.title: 03 Expanse: The Nannup Four | Down the rabbit hole
episodes.description: Dominique travels across the country to meet the two people who might be able to help her understand how Chantelle came to be living a reclusive life in a hidden corner of Western Australia, alongside a self-styled spiritual guru 18 years her senior.

episodes.title: 02 Expanse: The Nannup Four | Selling snake oil
episodes.description: A chance encounter in the streets of Melbourne in 1998 leaves a friend wondering what Chantelle McDougall has been pulled into. Dominique hears about the escalating pattern of control Simon Kadwill exercises over Chantelle.

episodes.title: 01 Expanse: The Nannup Four | The people in the blue house
episodes.description: When three adults and a child disappear without a trace from the isolated bush community of Nannup in 2007, it sparks disturbing theories about what might have happened.

episodes.title: Expanse: The Nannup Four
episodes.description: When four people disappeared from a blue farmhouse on the outskirts of the Western Australian town of Nannup in 2007, they left behind the scatterings of a life, a note pinned to their door and a question: was the disappearance a choice... or murder?

episodes.title: BONUS Expanse: Nowhere Man | Gunslinger
episodes.description: The search for Robert Bogucki brought together a cast of colourful characters, including a cigar-toting, moustachioed American named Garrison ‘Gunslinger’ St Clair.

episodes.title: 06 Expanse: Nowhere Man | Lost and found
episodes.description: A quarter of a century after he survived the Great Sandy Desert, Robert Bogucki is back for an odd-couple road trip with the Aboriginal tracker who helped search for him all those years ago.

episodes.title: 05 Expanse: Nowhere Man | Miracle in the desert
episodes.description: After almost six weeks in the desert, Robert Bogucki is found alive in what quickly becomes known as ‘The miracle in the desert’. But now he has to survive the tabloid television treatment and a fierce public backlash.

narrativeHook: A young American firefighter vanishes into the Australian desert, leaving behind a mystery that haunts those who search for him.

title: Global Roaming with Geraldine Doogue and Hamish Macdonald and Kylie Morris and Latika Bourke - ABC listen
description: Award-winning journalists Geraldine Doogue and Hamish Macdonald are joined by two new hosts, former foreign correspondent Kylie Morris and journalist Latika Bourke in London. Every day, they'll be discussing the biggest world events and how to make of sense of them.

episodes.title: A Matter of Facts: Wikipedia co-founder on freedom of speech vs disinformation
episodes.description: Is Wikipedia a relic of a more utopian version of the internet? Or is it the citizen-led antidote that we need?
episodes.narrativeHook: Wikipedia's co-founder debates whether the platform is a relic of the past or a vital tool against disinformation.

episodes.title: Could Australia and Asia supply our own energy and cut out the Middle East?
episodes.description: The Middle East conflict has triggered a reckoning in global energy supplies.
episodes.narrativeHook: Could Australia and Asia replace Middle East energy supplies in a post-conflict world?

episodes.title: Can Cubans survive under Trump's fist?
episodes.description: The war in Iran has aroused worldwide fears: what happens if a country runs out of oil? Because of severe US restrictions, Cuba has faced that reality, having been without oil for three months.

episodes.title: Trump and the Iran ceasefire: what happens next?
episodes.description: A ceasefire is declared after Donald Trump agrees to a two-week pause in attacks on Iran, contingent on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. But is this a genuine de-escalation or a strategic pause?

episodes.title: Soft power, hard lesson: what can Australia learn from unhappy Asian students?
episodes.description: Australia's education system is one of our most successful export industries, worth an estimated 54 billion dollars.

episodes.title: A Matter of Facts: How mainstream media lost public trust
episodes.description: In our previous Matter of Facts mini-series episodes, we covered why our brains are vulnerable to misinformation, and how disinformation is affecting democracies. Today, we examine the public's trust (or lack thereof) in mainstream media.

episodes.title: The lives of Australian diplomats: what it's like to be on the front line of world politics
episodes.description: Today, a special episode recorded at the Manly Writer's Festival 2026 where Geraldine speaks to three highly experienced diplomats -- Ian Kemish AM, Dr Robert Bowker, Dr Lachlan Straun.

episodes.title: Greater Israel: Is Netanyahu pursuing an expansionist dream?
episodes.description: As the war in the Middle East rages, Israel is waging offensives on multiple fronts. The state is pounding Iran and Beirut with missiles and drones. Ground troops are pushing deep into southern Lebanon and occupy half of Gaza.

episodes.title: Is Trump already past the point of no return in Iran?
episodes.description: Iran has withstood US and Israel's offensive more effectively than those who attacked it had expected. They've made the most of geography - and shown just how vulnerable the global economy is.

episodes.title: Will Japan be pulled into defending the Strait of Hormuz?
episodes.description: President Trump’s campaign to pull allies like Australia and Japan into defending the Strait of Hormuz is growing more urgent by the day.

narrativeHook: Award-winning journalists and new hosts dive into global events with insightful analysis.

title: Health Report with Norman Swan and Dr Preeya Alexander - ABC listen
description: Covering the health stories that make a difference. Dr Norman Swan and Dr Preeya Alexander dissect the latest and breaking news in the medical world.

episodes.title: Treating a medical emergency ... in space
episodes.description: When a medical emergency happens in space, how is it treated? And what does life in Antarctica have to teach us about staying healthy on a spaceflight?
episodes.narrativeHook: What happens when a medical emergency strikes in space and how does life in Antarctica prepare us for it?

episodes.title: What to expect this flu season
episodes.description: Which flu strains are likely to be dominant this flu season - and what's the story with the new nasal spray vaccine? Speaking of sprays ... there's a simple saline spray that might help kids with sleep apnoea avoid surgery.
episodes.narrativeHook: Discover the flu strains dominating this season and the new nasal spray vaccine's role.

episodes.title: 3D printing in healthcare
episodes.description: 3D printing is becoming an incredibly versatile modern tool - with scope to apply it to engineering, manufacturing, architecture and design challenges. And it's increasingly being used in ... healthcare.

episodes.title: Ultra-processed foods and behaviour in kids
episodes.description: There's been major buzz in recent years over ultra-processed foods and whether they may be harmful to our health.

episodes.title: MDMA therapy's side effects
episodes.description: MDMA psychotherapy was approved in Australia three years ago. Who's using it and what do we know about treatment side effects? Vaccine reminders can help nudge people back on track, but how the message is framed matters.

episodes.title: Are Australian kids eating too much salt?
episodes.description: Are Australian schoolkids eating too much salt? And does it put them at risk of high blood pressure? A new approach to breast cancer screening based on risk could reduce the number of screens needed for some women.

episodes.title: Can AI chatbots be good therapists?
episodes.description: We know many people are turning to generative AI for health advice, including tips on how to manage stress, anxiety and low mood.

episodes.title: Wait, does exercise help osteoarthritis?
episodes.description: A paper has suggested exercise has minimal, short-term effects on osteoarthritis. But experts are warning people with the condition that they shouldn't stop moving.

episodes.title: Prescribing exercise for mental health
episodes.description: Researchers have pin-pointed the best exercise routines for depression or anxiety symptoms, and they might be equal to medication and talk therapy. Also, why states and territories are making changes to their maternity care guidance for doctors.

episodes.title: The cost shock of specialist care
episodes.description: When you pay for private health insurance, you might assume you'll be well covered if you get injured or fall ill. But a new report has revealed the huge costs that catch people off guard, and sometimes prevent them from receiving care.

narrativeHook: Dr Norman Swan and Dr Preeya Alexander explore the latest in medical news and health breakthroughs.

title: If You're Listening with Matt Bevan - ABC listen
description: The world is on fire. There’s a coup. Inflation is through the roof, and AI is taking our jobs. What does it all mean? Each week, Matt Bevan explains the biggest story in world news while hiding in his basement from assassins and authoritarian regimes.

episodes.title: The brutal scam compounds of Myanmar
episodes.description: Over the past few years, industrial scam compounds have surged throughout Myanmar, buoyed by the resources of powerful criminal networks, and hidden by the chaos of civil war.
episodes.narrativeHook: Industrial scam compounds in Myanmar thrive on criminal networks and civil war chaos.

episodes.title: Growing up fighting apartheid
episodes.description: Sisonke Msimang from the new ABC podcast Boycott! joins Matt to share her father’s journey as a revolutionary in the fight against apartheid. Follow If You're Listening on the ABC Listen app.
episodes.narrativeHook: Sisonke Msimang recounts her father's revolutionary fight against apartheid in this gripping episode.

episodes.title: What happened last time we ran out of oil
episodes.description: Turn on the tv and you’ll see no shortage of concerned journalists standing at fuel bowsers, shaking their heads at the rising prices.

episodes.title: When Iraq accidentally bombed a U.S. warship
episodes.description: In 1987 the USS Stark became the first U.S. ship sunk by missile fire since World War II. The missiles were fired by Iraq, America’s ally at the time, who claim they did it by mistake. Follow If You're Listening on the ABC Listen app.

episodes.title: We were warned about the Strait of Hormuz
episodes.description: While governments scramble to find a way around the Strait of Hormuz, a pipeline sits half-finished in the desert that would have solved the problem. So why was it never completed? Follow If You're Listening on the ABC Listen app.

episodes.title: Why Iran is building their own internet
episodes.description: As we’ve been looking into Iran over this month, we’ve had a lot of trouble finding out what is really happening on the ground. That’s due to the concerted and deliberate internet shutdowns carried out by the Iranian regime.

episodes.title: Iran is running out of water
episodes.description: Water is the lifeblood of all civilisations. In Iran, the water is drying up. That disappearance is becoming impossible to ignore, and after decades of mismanagement, the country’s water system is approaching a breaking point.

episodes.title: Life inside the Iranian Revolution
episodes.description: Author Saeed Fassaie shares his story of witnessing the Iranian revolutionary first-hand, from being a political fugitive, to a soldier, to building a new life in Australia. Follow If You're Listening on the ABC Listen app.

episodes.title: Who is Trump really fighting in Iran?
episodes.description: There’s a persistent fantasy in Washington that regimes are like light bulbs: smash the fixture, screw in a new one, problem solved. The reality in Iran is closer to a tangled electrical grid that’s been growing since 1979.

episodes.title: Kylie Moore-Gilbert says Trump might be stuck in Iran
episodes.description: Australian academic Kylie Moore-Gilbert spent over 800 days in an Iranian prison interrogated by the Revolutionary Guard, and got into plenty of arguments while she was there.

narrativeHook: A journalist hides in his basement while unraveling global chaos and AI's impact on jobs.

title: Late Night Live with David Marr - ABC listen
description: Incisive analysis, fearless debates and nightly surprises. Explore the serious, the strange and the profound with David Marr.

episodes.title: The making of poet A.D. Hope, Australian literary giant
episodes.description: Alec Derwent Hope (1907–2000) was one of Australia's most acclaimed poets. His first collection was not published until he was 48 years old, but its release cemented his reputation as the pre-eminent Australian poet of his time.
episodes.narrativeHook: A poet's first collection published at 48 defines his legacy as Australia's literary giant.

episodes.title: Attacks on culture in the USA, plus the secret life of famous author Daniel Defoe
episodes.description: Pulitzer prize-winning art critic Sebastian Smee, looks at the state of the arts in Trump's America, and the story of Daniel Defoe's secret life as a spy, against Scottish independence, in the early 1700s, before he became the author of the famous…
episodes.narrativeHook: A Pulitzer prize-winning art critic explores Trump's America and Daniel Defoe's secret life as a spy.

episodes.title: Bruce Shapiro's USA, antibiotic resistance in India, plus Marralwanga's bark paintings
episodes.description: Bruce Shaprio on the US President's latest ultimatum for Iran. Prof.Assa Doron reveals how India has become the global epicentre for the world's antibiotic resistance problem.

episodes.title: Henry Reynolds turns Australian history upside down
episodes.description: The writing of Australian history has tended to focus on the south-eastern corner of the continent, but the story of colonisation north of the Tropic of Capricorn paints a vastly different picture of this country, its people, politics and ambitions.

episodes.title: Robert Reich's America, plus ten years since the release of the Panama papers
episodes.description: In his new memoir, Former Secretary of Labor under Bill Clinton, Robert Reich, traces how the Democrats lost the working class and paved the way for Donald Trump.

episodes.title: Ian Dunt's UK, and the Shahs and Ayatollahs of Iran
episodes.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces his plan to address fuel prices. And 'The Shah's party, and the Iranian revolution that followed'.

episodes.title: Western Australia's GST wins, Israel death penalty for West Bank, and mapping the wilderness
episodes.description: The only Australian state with a budget surplus will get an extra $6.6 billion from Australian taxpayers in the coming financial year, under its special GST deal.

episodes.title: Anna Henderson's Canberra, Ash Sarkar critques the modern Left, and should daylight savings be permanent?
episodes.description: The Australian government will halve the fuel excise for three months, as the energy crisis triggered by the Iran war looks set to drag on.

episodes.title: The struggle to get aid into the Middle East, plus a great Australian librarian retires
episodes.description: Millions have been made homeless by wars in the Middle East, but with access severely limited, humanitarian agencies are struggling to get aid into the region.

episodes.title: Bruce Shapiro's USA, Trump’s business in the Gulf, plus the Museum of Failure
episodes.description: Bruce Shapiro on whether Trump now looking for a way-out of the war in Iran, and why the Pentagon has lost its defence of media shut-out rules.

narrativeHook: Join David Marr for incisive analysis and fearless debates on the serious, strange and profound.

title: No One Saw It Coming with Marc Fennell - ABC listen
description: The bit players, the unexpected twists, the turning point you missed. Join Walkley award-winner Marc Fennell as he uncovers the incredible moments that changed the course of history.

episodes.title: Ancient Greek built a steam engine for dinner parties
episodes.description: Long before steam trains, before factories, before the Industrial Revolution, someone figured out how to turn steam into motion.
episodes.narrativeHook: Long before steam trains, someone used steam to power ancient Greek dinner parties.

episodes.title: She gave her son smallpox. Her bet paid off.
episodes.description: It was one of the deadliest diseases known to humankind. And just 50 years ago it was officially eradicated. But there’s someone missing from the story of smallpox.
episodes.narrativeHook: A mother's risky decision to give her son smallpox led to a pivotal moment in medical history.

episodes.title: Cocaine wine: The Pope’s energy drink
episodes.description: If you looked at it, you wouldn’t bat an eyelid, but this red wine had something in it that today could land you in jail. It was drunk and endorsed by presidents, royalty and even popes and made its maker a millionaire.

episodes.title: A horse race and a murderer invented cinema
episodes.description: Before cinema, before Hollywood, before we even understood how to make pictures move, there was a man constantly reinventing himself. He was a bookseller, a photographer, an alleged fraud and eventually, a killer.

episodes.title: Starving for freedom: The prison death that changed Ireland
episodes.description: As the Irish Revolution raged year after year, there was a space that the British didn’t expect to become places of revolution - prisons.

episodes.title: Let slaves dance: The secret of New Orleans jazz
episodes.description: When you put on a jazz record, what do you hear? Beyond the trumpet and the sax of course... Well etched into that vinyl and living in that music is a long story that dates back 300 years to a dusty public square where slaves would sing and dance.

episodes.title: She faked insanity. Then became a star.
episodes.description: She was put into an insane asylum at the age of 20. Ten days later she was a celebrity and two years later she had cemented a legacy that would last centuries. But Nellie Bly was not insane. She faked it all. But why?

episodes.title: The mafia bar riot that sparked gay pride
episodes.description: 28 June 1969 was a regular Saturday night at the Stonewall Inn. Until it wasn’t.

episodes.title: The royal roots of French fries

description: Corbin Middlemas and ex-Test opener Ed Cowan deliver you the best analysis in cricket with a rolling conversation on Australia's national game. This cricket podcast gets you across the Test format, T20 and ODIs with thought provoking conversation.

episodes.title: Straight up, this episode is MUST listen

episodes.title: T20 World Cups every two years just don't resonate

description: ABC News Daily is the podcast that helps you understand the issues affecting your world. Every episode, host Samantha Hawley walks through one story with the help of an ABC colleague or expert in under 15 minutes. When you want coverage you can trust, listen to ABC News Daily.

episodes.narrativeHook: Alan Kohler argues for nationalising childcare to remove it from for-profit control.

episodes.description: A fragile two week ceasefire between Iran, the United States and Israel has raised hopes ships stuck in the Strait of Hormuz will soon be on the move.
episodes.narrativeHook: A fragile ceasefire between Iran, the US, and Israel may ease congestion in the Strait of Hormuz.

episodes.title: Can Iran and Trump really agree on a peace plan?
episodes.description: Donald Trump was threatening to wipe out ‘a whole civilisation’, then about an hour before his deadline the US president announced a ceasefire deal had been struck with Iran.

episodes.title: Ben Roberts-Smith and the war crime of murder
episodes.description: As a Victoria Cross recipient, Ben Roberts-Smith is one of Australia’s most decorated soldiers. Now, he’s been charged with five counts of the war crime of murder.

episodes.title: Will Pete Hegseth take the fall for the Iran war?
episodes.description: We know that US President Donald Trump is the ultimate decision maker when it comes to the war in Iran, but who’s in his ear?

episodes.title: Are insiders profiting from the Iran war?
episodes.description: Oil and financial markets have been swinging wildly with every social media post from Donald Trump. But a pattern of large, well-timed trades placed on commodity and prediction markets just minutes before major Iran war announcements has emerged.

episodes.title: Will Trump escalate or end the war?
episodes.description: He's sending more troops to the Middle East, while insisting the war in Iran is nearly over. So is Donald Trump preparing to pull out or digging in?

episodes.title: Will there be enough fuel for Easter travel?
episodes.description: With the Easter break approaching, many motorists are wondering if they’ll be able to fill up their tanks and whether it’s worth travelling far from home.

episodes.title: Why Alan Kohler is worried about a recession
episodes.description: Could the Iran war lead our economy into a recession? Past oil shocks have sparked economic downturns and as petrol and diesel prices climb now, it could happen again.

episodes.title: Will the fuel crisis spark a switch to electric trucks?
episodes.description: With the Iran war sending the price of fuel skyrocketing, the trucking industry is amongst the hardest hit and the costs will be passed on to consumers.

narrativeHook: Stay informed with ABC News Daily's concise, trusted coverage of global issues.
